newsitem.title: USA: High-oil corn "rising star", acreage nearing 1 mln.
newsitem.headline: High-oil corn "rising star", acreage nearing 1 mln.

text.p: High-oil corn is the rising star among value enhanced grains with U.S. acreage that will near one million acres this year, officials said Monday at a U.S. Feed Grains Council conference.

Overall, farmers were likely to plant three to four million acres of specialty corns -- white, waxy, high amylose and hard endosperm, said Steven Hofing, of Agricultural Educaton and Consulting, commissioned to report on the crops.
"The real exciting action is in high-oil corn," Hofing said in projecting a doubling in planted acreage this year.
By comparison, about 400,000 acres of high-oil corn were planted in 1996 and 250,000 acres in 1995, Hofing told reporters.
"There is a tremendous shift in people moving to value enhanced corn."
The Feed Grains Council designed its two-day conference to focus on value enhanced grains, especially corn.

Council President Ken Hobbie said value enhanced varieties accounted for about five percent of U.S. feed grain exports. The share could reach 15-20 percent in five years, adding about $160 million in revenue to the export sales tally, he said.

"Everyone is beginning to see the value (of the crops)," Hobbie said, but they require a reasonably sophisticated buyer to use them. Asian buyers, particularly in Japan but also in South Korea and Taiwan, show interest in them, he said.
Dennis Denton of the Illinois Corn Marketing Board said "High oil corn is moving in" as a popular planting option.

"I would say it (high-oil corn) is the rising star right now," Hobbie said, although genetic engineering could create attractive new varieites that were especially suited to specific uses, such as livestock feeding.
Enhanced value grains command premiums of 30 cents a bushel or more over No 2 yellow corn.
Early results of tests on 1996 value enhanced corn showed quality roughly consistent with the preceding two years, although there was some decline in test weights.
During a breakfast with reporters, Hobbie said the conference was aimed at giving a "kick start" the development of a market for value enhanced grains.
